title: Strings, Unicode and indexing boundaries
outcome: Process text without confusing byte positions, Unicode characters and visible grapheme clusters.

exercises.title: Advance safely
exercises.task: Move from the first to the second character in the UTF -8 fixture.
exercises.answer: Adding one to a valid byte index can enter a multibyte character.

exercises.title: Count visible units
exercises.task: Compare characters and graphemes in the combining-accent example.
exercises.answer: A visible text unit can contain multiple code points.

exercises.title: Normalize deliberately
exercises.task: Apply NFC to the combining-accent fixture.
exercises.hint: Retain the original if exact provenance matters.
exercises.answer: Canonical equivalence is a specific Unicode relation, not arbitrary semantic equivalence.

exercises.title: Handle empty text
exercises.task: Check an empty string before selecting its first character.
exercises.expected: The empty case is identified explicitly.
exercises.hint: Do not assume every string has index 1.
exercises.answer: A parser or display routine needs a documented empty-input policy.

exercises.title: Choose offset units
exercises.task: Store offsets for a cited text passage.
exercises.expected: Name byte, character or grapheme units and the text version.
exercises.hint: The source representation determines valid boundaries.
exercises.answer: Offsets are only reproducible against the same representation and indexing contract.

exercises.title: Add a counterexample
exercises.task: Test an ASCII indexing algorithm with multibyte text.
exercises.expected: The invalid byte-index assumption becomes visible.
exercises.hint: Use an expected failure rather than silently deleting characters.
exercises.answer: A representative boundary fixture checks a mechanism that ASCII alone cannot exercise.
